From d99df02ff427f461102230f9c5b90a6c64ee8e23 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kevin Cheng <chengkev@google.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 03:33:26 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] KVM: SVM: Inject #UD for INVLPGA if EFER.SVME=0

INVLPGA should cause a #UD when EFER.SVME is not set. Add a check to
properly inject #UD when EFER.SVME=0.

Fixes: ff092385e828 ("KVM: SVM: Implement INVLPGA")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Kevin Cheng <chengkev@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Yosry Ahmed <yosry.ahmed@linux.dev>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260228033328.2285047-3-chengkev@google.com
[sean: tag for stable@]
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>

diff --git a/arch/x86/kvm/svm/svm.c b/arch/x86/kvm/svm/svm.c
index d82e30c40eaa..543f9f3f966e 100644
--- a/arch/x86/kvm/svm/svm.c
+++ b/arch/x86/kvm/svm/svm.c
@@ -2367,6 +2367,9 @@ static int invlpga_interception(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu)
 	gva_t gva = kvm_rax_read(vcpu);
 	u32 asid = kvm_rcx_read(vcpu);
 
+	if (nested_svm_check_permissions(vcpu))
+		return 1;
+
 	/* FIXME: Handle an address size prefix. */
 	if (!is_long_mode(vcpu))
 		gva = (u32)gva;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file, `arch/x86/kvm/svm/svm.c`, to add a permission check in the `invlpga_interception` function. The change ensures that when EFER.SVME is not set, the `INVLPGA` instruction triggers an `#UD` (undefined instruction) exception as required by the AMD architecture.

### Modifications in each file

- **arch/x86/kvm/svm/svm.c**: Added a call to `nested_svm_check_permissions(vcpu)` early in `invlpga_interception()`. If the check fails (i.e., EFER.SVME is 0 or other nested SVM permissions are not met), the function returns `1`, causing KVM to inject a `#UD` instead of executing the instruction.

### Relationships across files

The fix is self-contained within `svm.c`. The added call to `nested_svm_check_permissions()` reuses an existing function that validates SVM execution conditions (including EFER.SVME). This ensures that the behavior of `INVLPGA` matches the AMD specification, correcting the prior omission that allowed the instruction to proceed even when SVME was disabled.

Here is the commit message:
KVM: SVM: Inject #UD for INVLPGA if EFER.SVME=0

INVLPGA should cause a #UD when EFER.SVME is not set. Add a check to
properly inject #UD when EFER.SVME=0.

Fixes: ff092385e828 ("KVM: SVM: Implement INVLPGA")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Kevin Cheng <chengkev@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Yosry Ahmed <yosry.ahmed@linux.dev>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260228033328.2285047-3-chengkev@google.com
[sean: tag for stable@]
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>

Here is the root cause:
The `invlpga_interception` handler in KVM's SVM code did not verify that EFER.SVME is set before executing the INVLPGA instruction. Per the AMD architecture, INVLPGA is an SVM instruction that must cause a #UD when SVM is disabled (EFER.SVME=0). The missing permission check allowed the instruction to proceed unconditionally, violating architectural behavior.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int invlpga_interception(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu)
 {
 	gva_t gva = kvm_rax_read(vcpu);
 	u32 asid = kvm_rcx_read(vcpu);
 
+	if (nested_svm_check_permissions(vcpu))
+		return 1;
+
 	/* FIXME: Handle an address size prefix. */
 	if (!is_long_mode(vcpu))
 		gva = (u32)gva;
 
 	trace_kvm_invlpga(to_svm(vcpu)->vmcb->save.rip, asid, gva);
 
 	/* Let's treat INVLPGA the same as INVLPG (can be optimized!) */
 	kvm_mmu_invlpg(vcpu, gva);
 
 	return kvm_skip_emulated_instruction(vcpu);
 }
